units.title: Chandlery: diesel up again, new stock in
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: diesel up four pence a litre from today lads not my doing blame the tanker. new in: oilskins in the small sizes finally, shackles, the good bilge pump brushes, and a box of head torches that are better than the ones I sold you last year. tide tables for next quarter are on the counter, free, take one

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Rook, put two of the head torches aside for the boat please, the deck crew have been sharing one and it is not ideal on a wet ramp. I will pick them up before the 18:10. Also the small oilskins, one medium if you have it, for Finn, his has a split down the back.

units.title: Night run this week: drizzle and low cloud
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For anyone meeting the night boat. Forecast is drizzle and low cloud most evenings this week, visibility not as bad as the fog last week but patchy over the Lisle narrows. Expect the 21:15 and 22:40 to run five to fifteen minutes behind. We will sound on approach to both slips as usual. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine room report for the curious: number two genset has stopped weeping oil since I replaced a gasket that cost less than my lunch. Port engine is fine. The searchlight on the wheelhouse roof has a cracked lens, temporary fix with clear tape, proper part on order. It still throws a beam. It just throws it with character.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Passengers with bikes on the 21:15, please wait at the rail until the ramp is down and the deck crew wave you on. We had someone ride straight off the end of the Lisle ramp last week in the wet. He was fine, his pride was not.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: in fairness to bike man he did a lovely wheelie first and kerris gave him a talking to so stern he apologised to the bike, also cheers for the oilskin kerris i have been wet down one side for a fortnight and people have started standing on my dry side

units.title: Prices, Holm side, this week
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Brown crab steady, velvets down, buyer in Ammet says the restaurants are quiet before the holidays. Lobster fair. Lost two creels off the Holm side in the swell Sunday, found one on the shingle by the curing station wall. Other one's away. Weather looks dirty for the weekend, aye.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: bram if your creel washes up on the lisle side i'll bring it back on the boat, we've had a buoy and half a fish box come over this week already. the chippy has started doing crab rolls by the way and charging a fortune so someone is making money off you

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: bram I've got your old creel tags on file if the second one turns up, I'll ring you. weekend looks bad lads, get your gear lashed. and finn the chippy pays the same price for crab as everyone else, they're just better at selling it

units.title: Brackwater substation, last night: what actually went
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Since half the Sound Board think it was sabotage and the other half think it was squirrels. It was a failed bushing on the number one transformer, the porcelain insulator where the line goes in. Cracked, tracked, flashed over, breaker did its job. Flaming loud, I'm told. We had a mobile generator on the pumping station by midnight and the replacement in by mid-morning. Boring old age.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Garvey, two questions for the apprentice: how do you tell a cracked bushing from a dirty one when you're looking up from the ground at night, and was the crack from age or from the cold snap we had at the start of the month? I was on the Gilliver feeder when the call came and only saw it on the board.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Tess, from the ground at night you mostly don't, that's why we have binoculars and daylight. A dirty one has a brown glaze and you'll see a faint blue crackle in wet weather. This one was 1970s porcelain with a hairline that let the damp in. Cold snap might have finished it off. Age started it. You'll see the old one in the yard, it's on the bench.

units.title: Lisle slip tonight (probably nothing)
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: So... I don't usually post at this time, ha. After the 21:40 went, I was doing the pier lights and the chain across the ramp, in the drizzle. There was someone standing right at the end of the slipway, where the weed starts. Dark coat. I thought fisherman, they sometimes go down for the turn of the tide. I went to tell them the slip closes and when I looked up from the chain they weren't there. No torch going up the shingle either. Ha, anyway.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Ada, are you ok? Not taking the mick, genuinely asking, it's late and you're on your own on the pier. Could they have stepped off the side onto the rocks? The Lisle slip has that drop on the left where the old steps were.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: wait what slipway lol. is this the same tall man from the gilliver one. he gets about doesnt he, does he have a ferry pass. maybe he's just commuting

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I'm fine, Tess, thanks... locked up and walked home the road way, not the shore way. The old steps are on the left, yes, but they're fenced since the spring and I'd have heard the fence, it rattles. I'll look properly in daylight. Probably a fisherman who moves quietly, ha.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Four pence. Aye, I'll be out on what's in the tank then. Rook, keep me one of the head torches, the old one's strap is gone and I've been holding it in my teeth like a dog with a stick.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: torch is behind the counter with your name on bram. kerris yours are bagged, two torches one medium oilskin. lads please stop asking me to order the cheap bait from the mainland, it's cheap because it's rubbish

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: right lads, normally this sort of thing goes to the Sound Board. Ada works the Lisle pier so it stays here as a safety matter. stick to what you saw and where. kit, any more of the commuting jokes and you can take them to the Sound Board where they'll love you

units.title: Notice: Trespass on slipways (Byelaw 14)
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour Notice 11/3. Members of the public are reminded that under Harbour Byelaw 14 the slipways at Gilliver and Lisle are closed to pedestrians between sunset and sunrise, except for persons engaged in launching or recovering vessels. Slipways are steep, weeded and unlit at their seaward ends and are hazardous in poor visibility. Persons found on the slipways after dark may be asked to leave. Thank you for your cooperation. M. Quill, Harbourmaster.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Ada, a question rather than a theory: what would we expect to see if it were a fixed object? From the pier light, in drizzle, a mooring post or a marker pole at the end of the slip would read as a dark upright shape, and when you bent to the chain and looked up again your eye would lose it against the water. Is there a post at the seaward end of the Lisle slip?

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Useful, thank you, Garvey. For the record I'd have bet on salt deposition on the insulator rather than a crack, given the fog week. Damp plus salt is how most coastal bushings go. A hairline in old porcelain is the less exciting answer and probably the right one. I'll stop telling people at the pub it was the fog.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: For what it's worth: the Lisle pier lights are three sodium heads and one of them, the seaward one, has been cycling on and off for a week. When it's off, the last ten metres of the slip are basically black. I'm not saying that's what Ada saw. I'm saying someone should ring the council about that light before somebody walks off the end.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engineer's reading of Byelaw 14: we are now all trespassers every time we tie up after dark, except we're 'recovering a vessel', which I suppose we are, because the boat comes back every night. Sensible notice. Unlit seaward ends is the bit that matters.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: We had cleared Lisle by 21:48 and were in the narrows, so the boat saw nothing. Ada reported it to me by phone this morning and I passed it on to the harbourmaster, as we did with ours. I'm not going to speculate on a forum about what it was. Someone on a slip after dark is a safety matter. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Thank you, harbourmaster. The night crew will report anyone we see on either slip after dark, as we already do, with time and position. If people want to fish the turn of the tide, the breakwater is lit and safer. That's not a joke. It's where we'd rather you were.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Same as I said the first time, for anyone keeping notes. Gilliver: end of the slip where the water starts, dark coat, no light, standing still, too tall for a kid, didn't answer two hails on the loud-hailer. Ada says end of the slip, dark coat, no light, standing still. I'm not adding anything to that. I'm just saying it's the same list.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Fine by me. Closed after dark is how it should be. But nobody on the boat thinks this is about kids fishing. We hailed someone twice and they did not move. A sign on a post doesn't change that, it just means next time we can call it trespass instead of whatever it was.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Kerris, thank you, and I do take your report seriously. The notice is about what the harbour can do, which is keep people off the slips and get the lights mended. I have asked the council to repair the seaward light at Lisle and I've put a padlocked chain on the Gilliver slip at night from this evening. If anyone sees someone on either slip, please ring the harbour office, not just the forum.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: so if the tall man is on the slip after dark he's breaking byelaw 14 and the harbourmaster will ask him to leave, which honestly is the bravest thing anyone has said all week, quill please wear a hi vis when you do it so we can see you from the boat

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Ferrous, good question, I went and looked at low tide this afternoon. No post. There's a ring bolt in the concrete about two metres from the end, flush, and some weed, and that's it. There was a post years ago, the stump is still there, but it's about knee height... I measured it against my boot, ha. So not that, I don't think.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: kerris is now keeping a matching list, next week she'll have a spreadsheet like the dellow lot. i'm only messing kerris. but the boat's been weird all week, everyone looking at the slips when we come in, even the skipper, and he never looks at anything except the gauges

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: reposting the harbourmaster lads, read it properly. chain goes on the gilliver slip at sunset, key is with the harbour office and with me at the chandlery for anyone launching. if you're recovering a boat late, ring first. and finn nobody is wearing hi vis for your entertainment

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Ferrous, you'd have been half right, there was salt on it too, there's salt on everything this side of Tollinby. But the crack was the flaming reason. You can tell the pub I said so. Also tell them it wasn't the Holm crew pinching our power, which I've been asked twice this week.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Nobody from the boats goes down the slip after dark anyway, only to haul out, and you'd hear the winch. My father wouldn't stand on the end of it at night. Not because of anything, just because. Aye, the chain's a good idea.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Knee height stump, so not a figure. Seth's point about the seaward sodium light cycling is a good one though: if it went off while Ada was bent over the chain, anyone standing there would be gone from view instantly and could have walked up the right side in the dark. Not saying that's it. Just that a light going off is a good way to lose someone.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: chain on the slip lol. the tall man is going to be so annoyed. does he have to ring the harbour office first or can he just text. asking for a friend who is very tall and stands still a lot

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: finn's right the whole boat looks like meerkats when it comes in now. saw it from the chippy. like six heads turning at once. honestly worth the price of a ticket

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Thank you for checking, Ada, that's more than most people do. So: no post. Then my next most likely answer is a person, perhaps an angler who came down the shingle and went back up on the dark side when the light cycled, as Tess says. I'd add that people misjudge distance badly on a wet slip at night. The end of the slip may have been closer, or farther, than it felt.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Update, thank you all. The chain went on at Gilliver last night at 16:52 and was taken off at 07:40 this morning with no problems. The council electricians will look at the Lisle seaward light on Friday. Please, if you are joking about this, do it on the Sound Board. My office gets the phone calls from worried parents.

units.title: Night boat: last night, nothing to report
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Both crossings last night ran to time within eight minutes. Lisle seaward light was off on approach at 21:37, on again by the time we tied up. Gilliver slip chained and clear. Crew are fine. I've asked them to stop reporting every heron on the rocks to the wheelhouse, but I'd rather they reported a heron than didn't report a person.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: The heron in question was reported four times and is now known on the boat as Colin. Colin stands at the end of the Lisle slip and does not answer hails either. I'm keeping a tally. Searchlight lens part arrived, so the tape comes off tonight and the beam loses its character.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Finn, a list is how you report something so it doesn't change every time you tell it. That's the whole point. You can laugh at the spreadsheet. I'm the one who stood at the rail with the hailer. And the rest of you: Colin is a heron, he is about three foot, I know what a heron looks like. Enough.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Seth, you can keep the Colin tally as long as you don't put it in the log. The log is for things that matter. Also, the new torches are good, thank Rook. Bow lookout can see the full length of the Gilliver slip with them now.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Thanks Ferrous. I've been going over it... it could have been closer. I was looking down at the chain and the padlock was stiff and when I looked up the seaward light was on, I think, but maybe it had just come back. So it might have been someone walking up the dark side. I'd like it to be that. Ha. I'm doing the chain facing the water now, though.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: fair kerris, sorry. i only take the mick because it's either that or think about it and i've got another four nights on the bow this week. the spreadsheet is good actually. please don't tell anyone i said that

units.title: Before the weather comes in
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Pulled the Holm side string today ahead of the weekend, half full, mostly brown. Bringing the pots in close to the harbour wall till it blows through. Second creel never turned up. Buyer's paying cash Saturday if anyone's short. Aye, and the curing station wall's lost another stone on the seaward corner.

units.title: Weekend low: linemen on standby
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Heads up from the co-op side. The low coming in at the weekend looks a proper one, so we've got two crews on standby and the new bushing at Brackwater is in, touch wood. If your lights go, ring the fault line, don't post on here and wait. And if a line is down, it's live until we tell you it isn't. Stay well clear.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I'm on the standby rota for the first time, so expect lots of nervous questions from me. Garvey has given me a flask and a list of every pole on the Gilliver feeder that leans. There are more than I'd like. Gilliver folk, please tie down your wheelie bins, we spend half of every storm moving bins off lines.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: same advice to everyone lads, double up your lines on the inner wall, put fenders out, and take the outboards off the punts. last big low we had two dinghies go up the slip on their own and one through the chandlery window, which I'm still annoyed about

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: If the forecast holds we'll likely cancel the night runs on the worst evening, decided on the day with the Met Office inshore forecast. Ferry bulletin will have it first. Please don't ring the boat, we won't answer while we're working.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: ok ok calm down kerris i get it, colin is a heron, the tall man is not colin. noted. i'll stop. not because anyone told me to. it's just got boring

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: it's past midnight kit and your mother thinks you're asleep. off the forum. everyone else, this thread's said all it can for now, if anything new happens on a slip, report it to the harbour office first and post after
